sections.h2: Selling a house fast in Irvington
sections.html:
Irvington owners choose among an agent, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash offer on the house as it stands. All three need a township housing inspection before title changes hands. Since that inspection sets the schedule, start it the day you decide to sell.

With under a third of units owner-occupied, plenty of sellers here are landlords or heirs. Inspection fees grow with the count of dwelling units in the building.

  • Listing: a fit when the house passes inspection with little work and should appraise well.
  • Private sale: realistic only if you can run the inspection, contract and buyer financing yourself.
  • Cash sale: suits code violations, tenants or probate trouble, since the contract can be written around the house's condition.

Irvington is a small, dense township of 2.92 square miles in Essex County, with Newark to the east and Maplewood to the west. Population was 61,176 in the 2020 census and is estimated at 62,233 for July 2025.

It is a rental-heavy township. Owners occupy 29.6 percent of units, and the median owned home is worth $335,600. Median rent is $1,386 a month. Owners pay $2,489 with a mortgage and $1,026 without. Across 23,542 households, median income is $61,609. If several relatives share ownership of the house, a short written summary of the key dates keeps everyone on schedule.

Irvington's code makes it unlawful to sell, convey or transfer a building with residential units, or for a buyer to take title or possession, until a Certificate of Housing Compliance has been issued. The Department of Housing issues it after an application and an inspection. The online portal at irvingtonportal.us handles the application and the separate Fire Department inspection.

Irvington certificates and fees
CertificateWhen it appliesFee or term
Certificate of Housing ComplianceSale or transfer of a building with residential units$237 per unit up to three units, $116 per unit beyond three
Temporary certificateViolations that will not be fixed before closingNonrenewable, up to six months
Certificate of HabitabilityRenting a dwelling unit to a new tenant$98 per unit, $47 per reinspection, renewed every two years

For an as-is sale, the contract must be attached to the application and signed by both seller and buyer. If the inspection finds violations that stay unrepaired, the director may issue the temporary certificate, and the buyer then acknowledges the duty to fix them. Liability for skipping the certificate falls on both the owner and the purchaser.

The code exempts transfers between immediate family members, a property inspected within the prior six months, a purchase made to demolish the building and probate transfers to heirs under a will. Ask the Housing Department to confirm in writing how those exemptions apply to your sale. A denied certificate can be appealed in writing to the Business Administrator, who must decide within five business days.

sections.h2: Where to apply and who inspects
sections.html:
The Housing and Building office sits in the Municipal Building, Room 201, at 1 Civic Square. An evening housing inspector is available Monday to Friday from 5:00 to 9:00 p.m. and Saturday from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., which helps working owners schedule around a job.

  • Owners of any building in the township, residential or commercial, must give the Housing Department, Tax Collector and Tax Assessor their true home address and company address.
  • Vacant properties go through the Vacant Property Registration Program, with registration on the township portal.
  • Violation notices become orders if no written petition for a hearing is filed within 10 days, so respond to any notice quickly.
  • Fines under the property maintenance code run from $50 for a first violation to $1,000 for a fourth, which also requires a court appearance.

Irvington lies between Newark and the suburbs, so transit helps a listing. The Garden State Parkway passes through the center of the township with exits 143 and 144. Interstate 78 touches the southeastern edge at Exit 54, and County Road 509 is the main local road.

  • Buses: the Irvington Bus Terminal on Springfield Avenue is one of NJ Transit's busiest. Route 107 reaches the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown, and nine routes run to Newark.
  • Schools: Irvington Public Schools run pre-kindergarten through grade 12.
  • Business incentives: parts of the township lie in an Urban Enterprise Zone, which allows a reduced 3.3125 percent sales tax at eligible merchants. The area around the bus terminal is a state-designated transit village.

Every deed in Essex County's 22 municipalities goes through the county Register of Deeds and Mortgages. To contest an assessment, file Form A-1 with the Essex County Board of Taxation, normally by April 1. Further appeals go to the Tax Court within 45 days of the board's judgment.

The seller carries the state Realty Transfer Fee. At Irvington's median owned home of $335,600, the schedule for prices under $350,000 applies, reaching $3.90 per $500 on the slice between $200,000 and $350,000. A landlord who lives out of state files GIT/REP-1 and prepays 2 percent of the price or 8.97 percent of the net gain, unless an exemption on the form applies.

sections.h2: From contract to closing, step by step
sections.html:
File the application on the township portal and pay the per-unit fee. Then book the Housing and Fire inspections, using evening or Saturday slots if you work days. When the inspector lists violations, repair them or attach the as-is contract and request the temporary certificate. Let the title company know about any lien or open violation so it shows on the closing statement.

No lender means no appraisal, a real help when the repair list is long. The certificate, tax payoff and recorded deed still apply, so take your deed, a recent tax bill, a mortgage payoff letter and any lease to the closing.

If the house is inherited, tell the Housing Department early that a probate transfer may be exempt, and keep the will and letters of authority with your paperwork. Ask the Housing Department how long the certificate stays valid, so a delayed closing does not catch you off guard.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate to sell my house in Irvington?
faqs.a: Yes. The Township Code requires a Certificate of Housing Compliance before any building with residential units is sold, conveyed or transferred. The Housing Department issues it after an application and an inspection, and a Fire Department inspection is also required, both started on the township's online portal.

faqs.q: How much does the Irvington sale inspection cost?
faqs.a: The code sets $237 per dwelling unit up to three units in a building and $116 for each unit above three. Reinspections carry their own fee, so fix the listed items before the first visit and confirm current amounts with the Housing Department.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Irvington house as-is if it has violations?
faqs.a: Yes, with conditions. The as-is contract must be attached to the application and signed by both parties. If violations remain unrepaired at closing, the director may issue a nonrenewable temporary certificate lasting up to six months, and the buyer acknowledges in writing the duty to bring the property into compliance.

faqs.q: Are any Irvington transfers exempt from the certificate?
faqs.a: The code lists family transfers, a property inspected within six months before the transfer, a purchase for demolition and probate transfers to heirs under a will. Ask the Housing Department to confirm in writing that an exemption covers your sale.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded for an Irvington sale?
faqs.a: At the Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages, which covers the county's 22 municipalities. A title company or attorney typically files the deed together with the transfer fee affidavit and GIT/REP form, so you seldom visit in person.
